title: Implement RBACv2 conditional claims router and KMS multi-provider fallback shim
author: Aisha Thompson
body: Summary: Adds an RBACv2 conditional claims router that evaluates operator/service claims at request time and maps them to role templates with deterministic precedence. Also implements a KMS multi-provider fallback shim to allow per-region and per-tenant KMS preference with safe fallback behaviour and circuit-breaking. Includes an audit redaction pipeline that enforces deterministic redaction rules while preserving non-repudiation via detached signatures. Motivation: Customers running Private/Dedicated deployments asked for finer-grained operator delegations (ENG-2345) and improved KMS resilience across clouds. This change reduces incident risk when primary KMS endpoints fail and gives compliance teams deterministic, auditable redaction controls for sensitive fields. What changed (high level): - auth/claims-router: new runtime component that consumes operator/service JWT claims and policy templates. Supports conditional mapping (attribute expressions), explicit deny/allow, and an ordered precedence list to avoid ambiguous grants. - pkg/kms/fallback-shim: pluggable adapter that attempts configured KMS providers in order, with exponential backoff, per-tenant allowlist, and fast-fail circuit breaker after configurable thresholds. - observability/audit/redaction-pipeline: staged pipeline that applies redact rules, produces a redaction map (salted hash of removed fragments) and emits both redacted payload and signed audit envelope. - migration: DB migration to add operator_claims_mapping table and a small schema bump for service_metadata.kms_preferences. - tests: unit coverage for conditional expressions, integration tests exercising KMS fallback sequences (mocked), and e2e to validate audit envelopes roundtrip. - docs: design doc and upgrade notes added under docs/security/rbacv2-claims-router.md and docs/private/kms-fallback.md.
commits: 3 commits: 1) claims router core + interface + unit tests; 2) kms fallback adapter + integration mocks + circuit breaker; 3) audit redaction pipeline, migrations, docs and test fixes
review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice design. Two requests: make the precedence table deterministic for equal-score rules, and add metric labels for fallback reasons.
Aisha Thompson: Addressed — added explicit tie-breaker (creation timestamp) and metric 'kms_fallback_reason' with stable labels. PTAL.
Linnea Park: Request change: redaction pipeline should not drop context fields used by downstream billing. Please add allowlist and tests.
Aisha Thompson: Added redact allowlist and unit tests; updated docs to mention fields preserved for billing and billing test scenarios.
Marcus Osei: Approved after CI green. Left a minor nit about log verbosity which we can follow up in a small patch.
release_notes: Added RBACv2 conditional claims router to allow attribute-driven operator delegations; introduced KMS multi-provider fallback shim for increased resiliency and per-tenant preferences; audit redaction pipeline for deterministic, auditable redactions while preserving non-repudiation.
notes_for_ops: Upgrade path: run migrations in maintenance window. Default KMS fallback config is disabled; operators must opt-in by setting service_metadata.kms_preferences. Claims router is backward compatible — existing static RBAC bindings remain honored. To enable feature flags in Dedicated/Private, set feature.rbacv2_claims_router = true in config maps. Monitor metrics: auth.claims_router.evaluations_total, kms.fallback.attempts, audit.redaction.count. Ensure KMS providers have proper credentials before enabling fallback to avoid cascading failures.
